checks: Matched source bb74919333cc624f §§1–7. For d=1 a centered interval gives the bound and a saturated right shift forces λ≤1. For d≥2 AM–GM gives λ≤4Γ²<1, so a negative shift cannot be worse than its positive reflection, and nonatomicity gives zero shift by continuity.

Checked Theorems 1–2 and the s-affine density definition in the primary Fradelizi–Guédon article. The original projected probability is 1/d-concave by Brunn–Minkowski on preimages and has no atoms. Use the continuous constraint x↦x on a compact interval. The shifted three-CDF objective is affine and weakly upper semicontinuous. Each admissible Dirac has x≥0 and score at most one. The remaining extremizers are centered and have affine-power exponent d−1 on their one-dimensional support. The argument bounds a larger family than their additional moment restrictions. Primary source: https://perso.math.u-pem.fr/fradelizi.matthieu/pdf/localizationDCG.pdf

Checked the quantile integral for m, the midpoint inequality m≥(1+r)/2, Jensen and the Cauchy–Schwarz second derivative of m(R)^d. These give Γ≤p₀≤1/2 and ensure both thresholds are proper up to the supporting transition.

In the decreasing orientation the derivative of the two-term score changes from negative to positive at the displayed critical shift. Past the upper-support transition the score decreases to its constant branch. On the critical branch the numerator difference is concave in R and has nonnegative values at R=0 and R=R_*, the latter from G(2m−1)≥0.

In the increasing orientation the derivative is nonpositive up to the upper supporting threshold and nonnegative afterwards. Recomputed the degree-two derivative and all Bernstein minima for d=3,…,6 from exact rational polynomial expansion. The d=7 margin recomputes as 29669536175/6597069766656, and Γ decreases with d. The accepted quadrature proof supplies T≤1/6 for d≥7.
For the decreasing simplex marginal the cut height v satisfies v^d=1/(1+k) and 2a₀−v=kv. Both cuts are proper, and the exact ratio is k^(d−1). Expanding log(2a₀) gives the stated limit 4/e².

dependencies.hypotheses: The increasing affine-power law is exactly the accepted density d x^(d−1)/(1−r^d) on [r,1] with the same mean and inner CDF T=G(2m−1). The proof's quadrature estimate supplies T≤1/6 for every d≥4, hence d≥7 here.

overlap.comparison: Same ordinary centered convex-body marginals and same three terms, with coefficient 1/2. Its equality at a saturated shift does not give the larger optimal coefficient or the proper positive-shift simplex equality.
Its two-tail sum uses equal weights and has no extra central-tail term. It does not supply the optimal coefficient in this three-tail expression.

readability: The proof uses s both as the nonnegative shift and in the name s-affine for the localization class. These are separate, and the latter parameter is 1/d.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The proof establishes the largest all-shift coefficient, including the distinct affine-power orientations and an actual simplex equality at a positive shift.
